clue.text: Accelerate when favourite's back in the lead

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for favourite, with its possessive s, from right to left

parts.note: a favourite is a pet, so favourite's gives PET'S
a side that is in the lead is up

explanation.surface: A racing tip: speed up when the favourite returns to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up a pace or effort is to increase it, so the phrase is a synonym of accelerate.

clue.text: Shot in the arm in Washington, I collapsed

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, across Washington, I and collapsed

explanation.surface: A Washington visitor reports getting an injection and then fainting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot in the arm' reads as a literal injection; its 'in' is not the indicator, the second 'in' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative shot in the arm is a boost or pick-me-up, and so is a restorative drink or remedy.

clue.text: Clerical worker in dock, one dealing in drugs

parts.note: a pen is a protected dock, as in a submarine pen
a pusher sells illegal drugs

explanation.surface: An office clerk appears in the dock, charged with drug dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' suggests a courtroom, but it is the shelter for boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a disparaging idiom for an office clerk doing routine paperwork.

clue.text: Page about marvellous quickly assembled property

parts.note: re means about or concerning
fab is slang for fabulous, marvellous

explanation.surface: An estate-agent page describes a wonderful house that went up fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated house is built from factory-made sections and put up on site in very little time.

clue.text: Lark, notice, in flight

indicators.note: in places the word for notice within the word for flight

parts.note: flight, as in fleeing, is an escape
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A songbird spotted while flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lark' and 'flight' set up a bird, but the lark is a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of mischievous fun, and so is a daring adventure or prank.

clue.text: All, without exception, envy her sort? Some, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old order, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims everyone envies a certain kind of woman, then hedges to just some.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom refers to every single person with nobody left out, the same as all without exception.

clue.text: New picture frames charged originally at a reduced rate

indicators.note: frames puts the rearranged letters around the opening of charged, like a frame round a picture
new suggests the letters of picture are made over into a fresh order
originally picks the start of the word charged

explanation.surface: A newly framed picture was first sold cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PICTURE into CUTPRIE, and 'frames' puts C (charged originally) into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-price goods are sold at a discount, below the normal price.

clue.text: Courtyard built by Irishman I love?

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish man's name, short for Patrick
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An Irishman I adore built the courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the Irishman as a generic Pat.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area beside a house, like a small courtyard.

clue.text: Ring about second young lady's redundancy

indicators.note: about says the ringing word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them
Miss is the title of a young unmarried lady

explanation.surface: A phone call about a young woman's job loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' is a verb here, a phone call, not a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made redundant is a form of being let go from a job, a discharge from employment.

clue.text: Popular, a New York fixture, whatever happens

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sporting fixture is a scheduled event

explanation.surface: A popular New York fixture will go ahead whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means regardless or no matter what, an equivalent of whatever happens.

clue.text: Examine some graduate students

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to assess a few postgraduates.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to examine or check it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Truthfulness of account given by member of the clergy's office

parts.note: a curacy is the post held by a curate, a junior member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A report on how honest the accounts of a church office are.
explanation.definitionFit: Accuracy is correctness or exactness, close kin to truthfulness in a statement.

clue.text: Piece that is for one who's just started

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A chess piece given to a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a novice or newcomer, someone at the very start of a job or sport.

clue.text: State of Aunt Kath, regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words Aunt Kath, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A question about where Aunt Kath lives, or how she is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a condition, but it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, in the Mountain West.

clue.text: Best fruit for boss

parts.note: top means best
a banana is a fruit

explanation.surface: Choosing the finest fruit to give the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is an informal idiom for the most important person, the person in charge.

clue.text: Love fine route followed, naturally

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil grades
a course is the route taken

explanation.surface: Happily, the scenic route was taken, as one would expect.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means certainly or as expected, which is what naturally means as an interjection.

clue.text: Cinema worker in uniform reset the reels

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: reels means staggers about, so the letters of reset the are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cinema employee in uniform rethreads the film reels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reels' looks like film reels but is the verb to stagger.
explanation.definitionFit: An usherette is a woman who shows patrons to their seats in a cinema or theatre.

clue.text: Having few worries about a heartless whistle-blower

parts.note: C, for circa, means about

indicators.note: heartless drops the central letter of the word for whistle-blower

parts.note: a referee blows the whistle in a match

explanation.surface: Someone untroubled by thoughts of an unfeeling informant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whistle-blower' suggests an informer, but it is the match official; 'heartless' removes the middle E of REFEREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree describes a person untroubled by anxieties or responsibilities.

clue.text: Tackle a gutted plump fish

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides of plump, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Preparing a fat fish for the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' hints at fishing gear, but it is the verb meaning to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach a problem is to begin dealing with it, as is to tackle it.

clue.text: Support husband, advanced in years

parts.note: old means aged

explanation.surface: Caring for an elderly husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something up is to support it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cocktail made by male wearing waistcoat

indicators.note: the man is inside the waistcoat he is wearing

parts.note: a gilet is a sleeveless jacket or waistcoat

explanation.surface: A cocktail mixed by a barman in a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimlet is a cocktail of gin and lime juice.

clue.text: Specimen politician put into auction

indicators.note: put into places the politician inside the auction

parts.note: an auction is a sale
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician's memorabilia sent to auction as a specimen lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a representative specimen taken for examination.

clue.text: Guide the Italian aboard vessel

indicators.note: aboard puts the Italian article inside the vessel, as passengers are on a ship

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for holding things
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian steering a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot something is to steer or guide it.

clue.text: A radio broadcast about left and right in force

indicators.note: about wraps the shuffled letters around the left and right letters
broadcast means scattered abroad, so the letters of a radio are rearranged

explanation.surface: A radio programme about left and right wings being in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges A RADIO into RAIOAD, which goes 'about' LR; 'in force' looks like a phrase, but 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad someone is to coerce or push them into something, to force them.

clue.text: Steer clear of area containing nothing

parts.note: something void is empty, containing nothing

explanation.surface: Advice to keep away from an empty zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' looks like an insertion signal, but 'containing nothing' together means VOID.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to keep away from it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Nobleman given attention by lake

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: An aristocrat listened to beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount and below a marquess.

clue.text: Formal proposal concerning answer to problem

parts.note: re means concerning
a solution answers a problem

explanation.surface: A committee's motion dealing with how to fix a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A resolution is a motion formally put to a meeting for a vote.

clue.text: Severely criticise article on Roman temple

parts.note: to pan a play is to slate it in a review
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A critic slates a piece written about a Roman temple.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is a famous ancient temple to all the gods.

clue.text: In close, judge houses

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the word for judge contains the word for close

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A judge's houses in a cul-de-sac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In close' reads as nearby; 'In' alone is the definition, meaning fashionable, and 'close' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is fashionable, the same as trendy.
